To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

general, specific and combination of general and specific warm-up (Wu) increases slow stretch-shortening muscle performance (e.g. countermovement jump – CMJ), but only specific WUs increases fast stretch-shortening muscle performances.
general, specific and combination warm-up (Wu) increase slow SSC (i.e. countermovement jumps) muscle performance, and that only the specific WU increase fast SSC muscle performance.
general, specific, and combined WUs increase slow SSC muscle performance, but that only specific fast SSC muscle performance increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of general, and specific warm-up on explosive muscle performance in healthy subjects.
the effects of warm-up on explosive performance.
the effects of warm-up on the performance of explosive muscle actions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the type of WU (i) affects explosive muscular performance, (ii) depends on the type of muscular performance and (iii) is dependent on the type of SSC muscle actions.

a warm-up consisting of 5 min running and 5 min of stretching exercises increases slow SSC muscle performance and a warm-up consisting 5 min of specific fast SSC muscle exercises (jumping) increases both slow and fast SSC muscle performance.
general, specific and a combination of general and specific WU increases SSC muscle performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best warm-up is the one that best matches the specific demands of the sport or training session.
a general warm-up is not enough to improve explosive performance, and that specific warm-up is superior to general warm-up.

a specific warm-up is more effective than a general or a combined warm-up in improving the fast stretch-shortening muscle cycle performance, and a general or a specific warm-up are effective in improving the slow stretch-shortening muscle performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WU should include both general (i.e. aerobic and stretching) and specific (i.e. fast SSC muscle actions) exercises.
specific and combined WUs increase slow SSC muscle performance, but to increase fast SSC muscle performance, specific fast muscle actions must be performed.
the type of warm-up performed prior to an exercise session is very important.
